prompt: You know two sides of a triangle and the angle between them, and you want the third side. Which law should you use?
hint: The Law of Sines needs a side and the angle OPPOSITE it, as a matched pair.

hints.text: The Law of Sines needs a side and the angle OPPOSITE it, as a matched pair.
Here the angle you know sits between the two sides, so no matched pair exists yet.
That is the side-angle-side case, and it is exactly what the Law of Cosines is built for.

explanation: The Law of Sines needs a complete pair: a side together with the angle across from it. In the side-angle-side case you do not have one.
The Law of Cosines, $c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C$, is designed for exactly this arrangement.
The Pythagorean theorem is out because the triangle need not have a right angle.

alternativeExplanations.title: A quick decision rule
steps: Use the Law of Cosines when you know all three sides (SSS) or two sides and the included angle (SAS).
Use the Law of Sines when you have a matched side-angle pair (AAS, ASA, or SSA).
Once the Law of Cosines has given you one more piece, the Law of Sines usually finishes the triangle faster.
